sense: to the greatest degree: most beautiful, like most

terms.grammar: the superlative degree of an adjective or adverb (cārissimus, difficillimus), with a genitive or ex for the group
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. superlātīvus: nōmen, in the superlative degree (Charisius, Priscian)
terms.comment: Latin says “most” with the ending: difficillimus, the hardest; the group is in the genitive: rērum omnium difficillimās. The superlative also means “very”. With quam, “as … as possible”: quam plūrima, as much as possible (Quint. 11.2.41).

evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.5: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur
Plin. NH 8.29: animālium maximē ōdēre mūrem
terms.comment: With verbs, and with adjectives that make no superlative; also “above all”: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis (Cic. Fam. 14.18.2).

terms.gloss: most, very much (with verbs: be able, be worth)
evidence: Ps.-Publil. I 15: In sterculīnō plūrimum gallus potest.
terms.comment: Plūrimum posse, to have the most power (see a lot).

phrases.latin: ubi rēs didicerant rērum omnium difficillimās, tacēre audīreque
phrases.english: when they had learned the hardest things of all, to keep quiet and to listen

phrases.latin: suō enim quisque studiō maximē dūcitur
phrases.english: for each of us is led most by his own interests
of all animals they hate the mouse most

phrases.latin: Semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē.
phrases.english: Good advice is always missing just when it is needed most.
On his own dunghill the cock is most powerful.

phrases.latin: quārē et puerī statim, ut praecēpī, quam plūrima ēdiscant
phrases.english: so let children, as I advised, learn by heart as much as possible from the start

sources: Lewis & Short: superlativus · Lewis & Short: magnus (maximē) · Lewis & Short: plurimus

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius, loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-plinius, loci-publilius, loci-quintilianus, loci-cicero-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s. “Ps.-Publil.” marks lines from the later collections printed with him.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
